correctness.rationale: The exact segment projection mixed-volume identities reduce the quotient to the transverse radius divided by normalized support average. The two support branches meet at t=a; differentiating the radius-normalized angular integral cancels all boundary terms, leaving c_n/r^3 times an integral of a-t with strictly positive weight on (a,1), so the reciprocal is strictly decreasing. Beta integration gives both endpoint limits. Two-segment mixed volumes and multilinearity yield the exact zonoid coefficient, attained by orthogonal segments. All quantifiers n>=2 and 0<a<1 are covered; standalone numerical diagnostics confirm selected dimensions but are not used for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The originating 2026 paper proves only the universal canonical-witness simplex characterization. A published exact lens mean-width theorem already determines the support function and its mean but does not assert that the mean decreases strictly relative to the simultaneously shrinking transverse radius, nor identify this normalized strict monotonicity as the canonical Bézout witness profile. The sign integral and exact connection to the optimal two-zonoid coefficient are independently derived. A 2025 zonoid theorem is coarser and does not imply the exact profile. Residual risk: the known mean-width formula may have previously been combined with projection formulas to produce an unindexed equivalent normalization theorem.
residual_risks: The full earlier lens mean-width evaluation mathematically determines the denominator, making formula-only variations covered; the new claim is limited to strict normalized monotonicity and the structural sharp coefficient connection.
The monotonic normalized quotient may have been independently obtained in non-indexed or unpublished literature.
Best constant for arbitrary non-zonoid auxiliary bodies is not claimed.
